$comment: The supported browser API of DNS & Email Audit, from 0.6.0 onward. Spec §10, stage 2.
CHECKED IN, not derived. The whole point of this file is that it is a decision recorded
before the build was allowed to produce the surface, so that the surface can be compared
against something a person wrote rather than against whatever esbuild happened to emit.
A test that read the facade out of the bundle would agree with the bundle by construction.
Two members, from a 95-member surface. Derived from ACTUAL CONSUMERS, which is what review
round 2 asked for: analyzeDomain and checkConnectivity are the only two DnsAudit members
the application itself calls. 77 of the other 93 were used by tools/scoring.test.mjs and 4
by tools/backtest.mjs; both became direct ESM imports in Task 2.3 and need no global.
Asserted against BOTH the source module's exports and the built bundle's global, EXACTLY
and IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, by tests/build/parity.test.mjs. Neither may carry a name this file
does not list, and neither may omit one it does. The contraction from 95 members does not
pass merely because Task 2.7 permits the global surface to move.
Non-enumerable own properties esbuild's CommonJS interop adds to the namespace object.
Measured, not predicted: Object.keys() returns the two members above, and
Object.getOwnPropertyNames() additionally returns __esModule. It is listed here so that
the comparison can be exact on BOTH property views — an artifact that is written down is
a fact about the build, and one that is not is a surface nobody is watching.
